films.title: ADULT PROGRAMMING
films.description: Raul Roig's 24-minute HATE TV full-length documents Valencia through eight principal riders, a separately billed 28-name mix and closing footage from Javier De Pedro and Alex Ríos. Roig filmed and edited the complete independent film for HATE TV.
creditNotes: HATE TV's authorized complete-film description names eight principal riders, then preserves 28 labels under MIX, followed by Javier De Pedro and Alex Ríos; the same description formally credits Raul Roig for filming and editing and Polifeme for TV intros.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the film as a 24-minute 2026 independent work by Roig and corroborates the eight principal riders, while Free Skate Mag calls it a new full-length and specifically identifies the closing Javier De Pedro and Alex Ríos footage.

The MIX labels are retained exactly as first-party credits, including mononyms and the published 'Fuck You' label. No surnames, identities or part hierarchy are inferred, and the standalone Julio label is not merged with Julio Martínez without source support.
films.locationNote: Free Skate Mag and Cardiff Skateboard Club independently identify the film as a Valencian scene document; HATE TV is Roig's producing crew and rights-holder channel.
films.historicalContext: ADULT PROGRAMMING extends Raul Roig and HATE TV's Valencian VX documentation into a complete local full-length, combining a deep scene mix with a distinct closing passage for Javier De Pedro and Alex Ríos.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. Its blue distorted parental-control title frame is dedicated film artwork and the page carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: HATE TV's own channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and publishes its principal, mix and closing rider credits plus Raul Roig's filming/editing credit. YouTube reports channelId UCm6DnGDnhkME__pATkGlS4Q, a 1,465-second feature, April 21, 2026 publication, OK playability and permitted embedding.
Independent contemporary coverage calls ADULT PROGRAMMING a new full-length from Valencian VX filmmaker Raul Roig and identifies the Javier De Pedro and Alex Ríos closing footage.
Independent filmography classifies the work as a 24-minute 2026 film by Raul Roig, corroborates the principal roster and preserves the full first-party description.

films.title: High Roller III
films.description: Rafael Zulueta's 27-minute Madrid full-length unites 28 skaters from several crews, with additional footage from Lisbon, Valencia, Alicante, Marbella and Bilbao. The filmmaker's complete upload supplies a timestamped appearance roster from Alonso de Arístegui through Chechu Rodríguez.
creditNotes: Rafael Zulueta's authorized complete-film description timestamps all 28 credited skaters in appearance order and identifies the work as his video.

Skate Jawn independently calls High Roller III a full-length filmed and edited by Zulueta, names the principal cast and documents the six-city Spain/Portugal footprint; SkateVideoSite independently corroborates all 28 skaters.
The official timestamps include one five-skater shared section, followed by individually timed appearances. No unsupported solo-part hierarchy is assigned beyond those published timestamps.
films.locationNote: Skate Jawn explicitly documents Madrid as the center of production and Lisbon, Valencia, Alicante, Marbella and Bilbao as additional filming locations; SkateVideoSite independently tags both Spain and Portugal.
films.historicalContext: The third High Roller film became a cross-crew Madrid project that Zulueta described as organically turning several previously separate crews into one family, while extending the footage across Spain and Portugal.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. Its motion-blurred night street frame is the official full-film image and the page carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Rafael Zulueta's own channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and publishes a timestamped 28-skater roster. YouTube reports channelId UCAMd5CCH7yBkyp7tNj1A_aA, a 1,618-second feature, May 11, 2026 publication, OK playability and permitted embedding.

Independent contemporary coverage calls High Roller III a full-length filmed and edited by Rafael Zulueta, names principal riders and documents Madrid, Lisbon, Valencia, Alicante, Marbella and Bilbao.
Madrid's Welcome Skateshop carries Zulueta's exact player and identifies the work as his video one day after its release.
Independent filmography classifies the work as a 27-minute 2026 independent film by Rafael Zulueta, corroborates all 28 riders and records both Spain and Portugal.

films.title: dumb bunny
films.description: Braeley Wong and Chance Swainson's 18-minute independent film follows 21 skaters through Vancouver, Victoria and the wider Pacific Northwest. The filmmakers' complete upload preserves the full order of appearance, timestamped sections and two additional camera credits.

officialTimestampedSections: Ty Peterson / Aleka Lang / Tremaine Glasgow
David Barbeau / Braeley Wong / Simon Richards
Matt Munn / Maxwell Norman Miller / Jordan King / Carter Lee / Brantyn Wong

creditNotes: Chance Swainson's authorized complete-film description names all 21 skaters in order of appearance, credits Braeley Wong and Swainson for filming and editing, and identifies Angelo Fajardo and Carter Spinks for additional filming.

SkateVideoSite independently corroborates the complete roster, four camera contributors, seven-section soundtrack and Vancouver/Victoria setting; Adjacency Bias independently identifies Wong and Swainson as the filmmakers and Dylan Timmins as the closing part.

Although SkateVideoSite catalogued the film as 2026, the official source was published December 16, 2025 and Adjacency Bias selected it among the top Northwest videos of 2025, so the canonical release year follows the documented first release.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite documents Vancouver and Victoria, while Adjacency Bias says the film was primarily shot in those cities with additional footage from across the Pacific Northwest.
films.historicalContext: Released at the end of 2025, dumb bunny quickly became one of Adjacency Bias's five favorite Northwest videos of the year for its crusty regional spots, cohesive scene identity and Dylan Timmins's closing part.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. Its high-contrast bunny image is dedicated film artwork and the page carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Co-filmmaker Chance Swainson's own channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and publishes the full 21-skater appearance order, section timestamps and complete camera/editing credits. YouTube reports channelId UCxp6AJJzs891hshkjL92TGg, a 1,050-second feature, December 16, 2025 publication, OK playability and permitted embedding.

Independent regional coverage names Wong and Swainson, documents the Vancouver/Victoria and wider Northwest setting, identifies Dylan Timmins as the closing part and selects the film among its top five Northwest videos of 2025.

Independent filmography classifies the work as an 18-minute film, corroborates all 21 skaters, both filmmakers, both additional camera contributors and the Vancouver/Victoria locations, while assigning a later catalogue year than the documented release.
